tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

on:

permissions: {}

jobs:
  retired:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Stop the retired docs operation
        shell: bash
        run: |
          printf '%s\n' 'The old documentation deployment is retired in this checkout.'
          printf '%s\n' 'Recovery: docs/documentation-audit/clean-slate-foundation/2026-10-07-docs-retirement-manifest.json'

name: Docs Deployment Workflow Receipts

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows:
      - Docs Preview Deployment
      - Docs Production Deployment
      - Docs Preview Teardown
    types: [completed]

permissions:
  contents: read
  actions: read

concurrency:
  group: taxkit-docs-workflow-receipt-${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  reconcile:
        env:
          DOPPLER_CONFIG: ${{ steps.doppler-ci.outputs.DOPPLER_CONFIG }}
          DOPPLER_PROJECT: ${{ steps.doppler-ci.outputs.DOPPLER_PROJECT }}
        run: test "$DOPPLER_PROJECT" = "taxkit" && test "$DOPPLER_CONFIG" = "ci"

      - name: Validate completed workflow input and run identity
        if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
        env:
          TAXKIT_WORKFLOW_INPUT_RECEIPT: ${{ runner.temp }}/docs-deployment/workflow-input.json
          TAXKIT_WORKFLOW_INPUT_RUN_ID: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
          TAXKIT_WORKFLOW_RUN_RECEIPT: ${{ runner.temp }}/docs-deployment/workflow-run-candidate.json
          TAXKIT_WORKFLOW_RUN_ID: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
          TURBO_CACHE: local:rw,remote:rw
          TURBO_TEAM: ${{ steps.doppler-ci.outputs.TURBO_TEAM }}
          TURBO_TOKEN: ${{ steps.doppler-ci.outputs.TURBO_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          input="$RUNNER_TEMP/docs-deployment/workflow-input.json"
          export TAXKIT_WORKFLOW_INPUT_CANDIDATE_COMMIT="$(jq -er .candidateCommit "$input")"
          export TAXKIT_WORKFLOW_INPUT_WORKFLOW_COMMIT="$(jq -er .workflowCommit "$input")"
          export TAXKIT_WORKFLOW_INPUT_WORKFLOW_PATH="$(jq -er .workflowPath "$input")"
          export TAXKIT_WORKFLOW_INPUT_OPERATION="$(jq -er .operation "$input")"
          export TAXKIT_WORKFLOW_INPUT_PR_NUMBER="$(jq -r '.prNumber // empty' "$input")"
          export TAXKIT_WORKFLOW_RUN_CANDIDATE_COMMIT="$TAXKIT_WORKFLOW_INPUT_CANDIDATE_COMMIT"
          export TAXKIT_WORKFLOW_RUN_WORKFLOW_COMMIT="$TAXKIT_WORKFLOW_INPUT_WORKFLOW_COMMIT"
          export TAXKIT_WORKFLOW_RUN_WORKFLOW_PATH="$TAXKIT_WORKFLOW_RUN_PATH"
          export TAXKIT_WORKFLOW_RUN_WORKFLOW_NAME="$TAXKIT_WORKFLOW_RUN_NAME"
          export TAXKIT_WORKFLOW_RUN_EVENT="$TAXKIT_WORKFLOW_RUN_EVENT"
          export TAXKIT_WORKFLOW_RUN_HEAD_BRANCH="$TAXKIT_WORKFLOW_RUN_HEAD_BRANCH"
          export TAXKIT_WORKFLOW_RUN_HEAD_SHA="$TAXKIT_WORKFLOW_RUN_HEAD_SHA"
          bun run check:docs-deployment-workflow-input
          bun run check:docs-deployment-workflow-run

      - name: Promote the validated workflow receipt
        if: success() && github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mv "$RUNNER_TEMP/docs-deployment/workflow-run-candidate.json" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/docs-deployment/workflow-run.json"

      - name: Retain bounded reconciliation stop when positive proof is unavailable
        if: always()
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ ! -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/docs-deployment/workflow-run.json" ] && [ ! -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/docs-deployment/workflow-run-failure.json" ]; then
            rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/docs-deployment/workflow-run-candidate.json"
            jq -nS \
              --arg conclusion "$SOURCE_RUN_CONCLUSION" \
              --arg run "$SOURCE_RUN_ID" \
              '{conclusion:$conclusion,nonClaim:"The completed source run could not be reconciled into a strict positive receipt; external state remains unestablished.",schemaVersion:1,workflowRunId:$run}' \
              > "$RUNNER_TEMP/docs-deployment/workflow-run-failure.json"
          fi

      - name: Prepare the allowlisted receipt upload
        if: always()
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          upload="$RUNNER_TEMP/docs-deployment-upload"
          rm -rf "$upload"
          mkdir -p "$upload"
          if [ -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/docs-deployment/workflow-run.json" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/docs-deployment/workflow-run.json" "$upload/workflow-run.json"
          else
            test -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/docs-deployment/workflow-run-failure.json"
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/docs-deployment/workflow-run-failure.json" "$upload/workflow-run-failure.json"
          fi
          test "$(find "$upload" -type f | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" = "1"

      - name: Upload reconciled workflow receipt
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7
        with:
          name: taxkit-docs-workflow-receipt-${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/docs-deployment-upload
          retention-days: 30
          if-no-files-found: error
      - run: apps/web/node_modules/.bin/playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - uses: actions/cache/save@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        if: steps.playwright-cache-restore.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          path: ${{ env.PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH }}
          key: ${{ steps.playwright-cache-restore.outputs.cache-primary-key }}
      - run: bun run check:quality-workflow
      - name: Fetch trusted CI configuration
        id: doppler-ci
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
        uses: dopplerhq/secrets-fetch-action@451892f16195f9ac360e1a5bcbf0b5fd0e957534 # v2.0.0
        with:
          doppler-token: ${{ secrets.DOPPLER_CI_TOKEN }}
      - name: Check trusted CI configuration identity
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
        env:
          DOPPLER_CONFIG: ${{ steps.doppler-ci.outputs.DOPPLER_CONFIG }}
          DOPPLER_PROJECT: ${{ steps.doppler-ci.outputs.DOPPLER_PROJECT }}
        run: test "$DOPPLER_PROJECT" = "taxkit" && test "$DOPPLER_CONFIG" = "ci"
      - name: Run trusted Quality with remote cache
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
        env:
          TURBO_CACHE: local:rw,remote:rw
          TURBO_TEAM: ${{ steps.doppler-ci.outputs.TURBO_TEAM }}
          TURBO_TOKEN: ${{ steps.doppler-ci.outputs.TURBO_TOKEN }}
        run: bun run release:check -- --ci
      - name: Run fork Quality without credentials
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository
        env:
          TURBO_CACHE: local:rw
        run: bun run release:check -- --ci

content.text:
The core finding is that most of this tooling only checks itself. There is one real exception: the docs catalogue build. The public docs catalogue is generated only after acceptance records and source hashes pass, and the API and web app both read that catalogue. Everything below is from reading files; I ran no scripts.

## 1. `verification` root script chain (24 steps, run in order)

| # | Script | Runs | Kind |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | check:oxlint:types | tsc on `tools/oxlint` | Real |
| 2 | check:repository-paths:types | tsc on `tools/repository-paths` | Real (small) |
| 3 | check:repository-paths | scans `git ls-files` for absolute home or checkout paths | Real hygiene check |
| 4 | check:harness-governance | `tools/governance/check.runtime.ts` | Ceremony |
| 5 | check:quality-workflow:types | tsc | Ceremony |
| 6 | check:quality-workflow | checks the shape of `quality.yml` against `controls.json` and `automation-register.json` | Ceremony |
| 7 | check:docs:types | tsc on `tools/documentation` (turbo makes it wait for the docs-content build) | Mixed |
| 8 | check:harness-foundation-epoch:types | tsc on `tools/evals` | Ceremony |
| 9 | check:docs | `tools/documentation/check.runtime.ts` | Mixed (see §4) |
| 10 | check:runbooks | `runbook-check.runtime.ts` (HGI-203/204 hashes) | Ceremony |
| 11 | check:effect-language-service | effect-tsgo diagnostics plus tsc on a 17-line `compatibility.ts` | Smoke test only; low value but not ceremony |
| 12 | check:docs-deployment:types | `tsc -p tsconfig.alchemy.json`, which covers `alchemy*.run.ts` and `packages/infrastructure/src/**` | **Real, despite the name.** Mostly duplicates infrastructure's own `check-types`, but the `alchemy*.run.ts` files are only covered here |
| 13 | check:docs-deployment-tools:types | tsc on `tools/docs-deployment` | Ceremony |
| 14 | check:docs-deployment | `tools/docs-deployment/check.runtime.ts` (about 30 receipts under `docs/evidence/deployments/**` plus `docs/verification/docs-deployment-journeys.json`) | Ceremony |
| 15 | check:docs-deployment-automation | `automation.check.runtime.ts` plus `automation-register.json` | Ceremony |
| 16 | test:docs-deployment | vitest on `tools/docs-deployment` | Ceremony |
| 17 | lint | oxlint (boundary-directive pass, then full) | Real |
| 18 | format:check | oxfmt | Real |
| 19 | test:hgi-206 | vitest on `tools/evals/hgi-206` | Ceremony |
| 20 | test:quality-workflow | vitest on `tools/quality-workflow` | Ceremony |
| 21 | knip | turbo makes it wait for the docs-content build | Real |
| 22 | knip:production | same | Real |
| 23 | check-types | turbo across workspaces | Real |
| 24 | sdk:test:browser, web:test:browser, `--filter=web check:worker-types`, web:test:native-pair | | Real |

`release:check -- --ci` is defined in `packages/scripts/src/release-readiness/schemas.ts` (`createReleaseReadinessPlan`). It runs `verification`, `test`, `build`, `docs:validate`, `sdk:check-packed-artifact`, `sdk:validate-downstream`, `api:smoke`, `web:test:native-pair` and `changeset:status`. In CI mode it writes no evidence. Running it without `--ci` reads `docs/evidence/releases/HGI-203-local.json` and builds a release-attempt receipt. Note that `web:test:native-pair` runs twice: once inside `verification` and again in the plan.

The root `test` script runs `test:documentation`, `test:repository-paths`, `test:oxlint`, then `turbo run test`.

## 2. Workflows (`.github/workflows`)

- **`docs-preview.yml`, `docs-production.yml`, `docs-production-hosted-verify.yml`, `docs-preview-teardown.yml`** (18 lines each): manual-only stubs named "… (retired)" that print a recovery pointer and `exit 1`. Nothing consumes them; nothing to keep.
- **`docs-deployment-workflow-receipts.yml`** (270 lines): fires on completion of workflows named "Docs Preview Deployment", "Docs Production Deployment" and "Docs Preview Teardown". Those names no longer exist (all now end in "(retired)"), so **this workflow can never trigger**. It runs `check:docs-deployment-workflow-input`, `check:docs-deployment-workflow-run` and a Doppler fetch. Nothing to keep.
- **`quality.yml`** (86 lines, PR plus push): installs, then runs `check:quality-workflow`, a Doppler identity check, and `release:check -- --ci`. **Keep.** Only the `check:quality-workflow` step is ceremony, and `tools/quality-workflow/policy.ts` checks this file's exact step layout, so editing `quality.yml` will break that check until it is retired.

## 3. tools/

**`tools/docs-deployment`** (860K, about 17.8k lines of TS). The retired docs deployment: Doppler custody, inventory, workflow input/run/plan/proof receipts, retirement refusal, plus fixtures.
- Consumers:
  - Root `package.json`: about 20 scripts (`check:docs-deployment*`, `check:doppler-custody`, `docs:dev:cloudflare*` (which run `retirement.runtime.ts`), `test:docs-deployment`).
  - `turbo.json`: 10 `//#check:docs-deployment*` tasks.
  - The receipts workflow.
  - `knip.json` entry/project lists.
  - `oxlint.config.ts`: about 100 path entries and override blocks.
  - `tools/oxlint/portable-rules.test.ts`: lines about 612–771 and 1313–1327 require exact override entries per file, so that test must be edited.
  - `README.md` (`check:doppler-custody`).
  - `packages/infrastructure/README.md` (lines 39 and 237).
- **App-stack tests read its fixtures.** `packages/infrastructure/src/apps-stack.test.ts` lines 335 and 365 read `tools/docs-deployment/fixtures/alchemy-beta.80/native-apps-preview.txt` and `native-apps-production.txt` as expected native-apps plan snapshots. These two files must move, for example into `packages/infrastructure`. The `alchemy-beta.64/*` fixtures and `fake-doppler*` are used only inside docs-deployment.
- No production code imports it.

**`tools/governance`** (80K). Checks `docs/verification/repository-harness-profile.json` and `critical-journeys.json`, `docs/documentation-audit/harness-foundation/{audit,accepted}-findings.json`, `docs/product-specs/harness-foundation-improvements*`, and that `package.json#scripts.verification` calls `check:harness-governance` exactly once.
- Consumers: `verification` step 4, `test:harness-governance`, `check:harness-governance:types`, turbo task, the oxlint runtime allow-list plus `portable-rules.test.ts`.
- Nothing kept depends on it.

**`tools/evals`** (176K): the `hgi-206/` and `harness-foundation/` checkers plus `hgi-206-*.json` and `harness-foundation-*.json`. They read `docs/documentation-audit/{hgi-206,harness-foundation}/**` receipts, epoch candidates and `HFI-004-candidate-*`.
- Consumers: `check:hgi-206`, `test:hgi-206` (in `verification`), `check:harness-foundation-epoch`, `check:harness-foundation-epoch:types` (in `verification`), oxlint config plus `portable-rules.test.ts`.
- Nothing kept depends on it.

**`tools/quality-workflow`** (132K): policy over the shape of `quality.yml`, `controls.json`, `automation-register.json` and its fixtures. It references `packages/scripts/src/release-readiness/*` as a control owner.
- Consumers: `quality.yml` step, `verification` steps 5, 6 and 20, `knip.json`, oxlint.
- Nothing kept depends on it.

**`tools/repository-paths`** (32K): rejects machine-specific absolute paths in tracked files. **A real check; worth keeping.**

**`tools/effect-language-service`** (8K): one trivial file used to smoke-test the effect-tsgo plugin (`verification` step 11, `knip.json` entry). Low value but harmless.

**`tools/documentation`**, split by usefulness:
- **Useful checks:** `policy.ts` and `check.runtime.ts` invariants `maintainer-metadata`, `lifecycle-successor`, `relative-link`, `local-bun-command` (a `bun run X` in docs must exist as a script), `workspace-readme`, `generated-source-owner`.
- **Ceremony inside the same files:**
  - The `owner-policy` invariant: requires one acceptance-record binding per published page and verifies `sourceSha256` through `verifyAcceptedSource`.
  - `DocumentationReceipt` with its nonClaim/postcondition fields.
  - The report written to `tmp/docs-policy-report.json`.
- **`owner-policy.json`** (319 lines) is mixed. Path classes (public, maintainer and sdkDocs roots, fumadocs, openApi bindings) are useful. `public.statusDecision.acceptanceRecords[]`, which maps each MDX page and `navigation.json` to `docs/documentation-audit/clean-slate-foundation/public-content-acceptance/2026-10-0{6,7,8}/*.json` (284K), is ceremony.
- **Pure ceremony:**
  - `runbook-contract.json` (HGI-204).
  - `runbook-policy.ts`, which imports types from `@taxkit/scripts/release-readiness`. This is the only code import of `@taxkit/scripts` anywhere.
  - `runbook-check.runtime.ts`, which hashes the `HGI-203-*` evidence and reads `docs/runbooks/*` and `docs/operations/authority-model.md`.
- **`catalogue.build.ts`, `catalogue.runtime.ts`, `catalogue.policy.ts`: needed for the real build** (see §4).

## 4. Docs packages

**`packages/docs-content`.**
- `generate` runs `fumadocs-mdx` and `src/catalogue-index.runtime.ts`. No ceremony.
- **`build` runs `generate` and then `tools/documentation/catalogue.runtime.ts`**, which:
  1. reads the acceptance bindings in `owner-policy.json`;
  2. decodes each `PublicPageAcceptanceRecordV2`;
  3. compares SHA-256 hashes of each MDX file and `navigation.json` against the record's `sourceSha256`;
  4. calls `projectPublicCatalogue`, which requires exactly one record per page with `status: "published"` plus navigation, else fails;
  5. re-checks the hashes, then writes `.source/public-catalogue.json`.
- The build therefore **depends on acceptance records and source hashes**.
- `turbo.json` `@taxkit/docs-content#build` lists `tools/documentation/catalogue.*`, `schemas.ts`, `owner-policy.json` and the `public-content-acceptance/**/*.json` files as inputs.
- **Consumers that must keep working:**
  - `apps/api/src/content.boundary.ts` imports `@taxkit/docs-content/public-catalogue`.
  - `apps/web/scripts/docs-images.build.ts` reads it.
  - `apps/web/test/native-pair.boundary.test.ts` (line 408) reads it.
  - `knip` and `check:docs:types` wait on this build.
  - The root `docs:catalogue` script.
- **Implication:** retiring acceptance records means rewriting catalogue build/policy to filter on frontmatter `status: published` alone. The projection logic (published filter, navigation pruning, parent/child check) is worth keeping.
- `docs:validate` (`src/validate.runtime.ts`, `src/validation/*`: MDX component policy and checked snippets) is real content validation. Keep it.

**`packages/docs-fumadocs`**: no acceptance, receipt or hash code. Nothing to retire.

**`packages/content/src/schemas.ts` lines 233–261**: `PublicPageAcceptanceRecordV1`/`V2`, `DocsAcceptedSourceDigest` and the `PublicPageAcceptanceRecord` union.
- Consumers: `tools/documentation/{schemas,catalogue.build,catalogue.policy}.ts` and their tests, and `packages/content/test/schemas.test.ts` (lines 88–96).
- No app imports them.

## 5. `packages/scripts` (release-readiness, 3.8k lines)

- `release:check` runs `release-readiness.runtime.ts`. `release:present` runs `present.runtime.ts`, which reads and verifies a release-attempt receipt.
- Consumers:
  - Root scripts `release:check`, `release:present`, `test:release-readiness`.
  - `quality.yml` (`release:check -- --ci`). **The ordered check plan is the real CI gate.**
  - `tools/documentation/runbook-policy.ts` (type import).
  - `tools/quality-workflow/{policy.ts,controls.json}`.
  - Both knip configs (`knip.production.json` also ignores exports in `evidence.boundary.ts`).
  - `oxlint.config.ts` and `portable-rules.test.ts` runtime allow-list.
  - Changesets, `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` (lines 24 and 104).
  - Root `devDependencies`.
- **Keep:** the plan of checks plus the CI runner (`program.ts`, `live.layer.ts`, `service.ts`, part of `schemas.ts`).
- **Ceremony:** `evidence.boundary.ts` (612 lines), `present.runtime.ts`, `output-redaction.ts`, local attempt receipts, the `ReleaseProofPacket` (`taskId: "HGI-203"`) and `docs/evidence/releases/HGI-203-*`.

## 6. Other dependents

- **`alchemy.run.ts`** exports `RetiredDocsStack`, defined in `packages/infrastructure/src/retired-stack.schemas.ts`. The record is a literal pointing at `docs/documentation-audit/clean-slate-foundation/2026-10-07-docs-retirement-manifest.json`. The retired workflow stubs print the same path. It is a string literal, not a file read.
- **`packages/content/package-structure.render.json`** and **`packages/api/rpc/package-structure.render.json`** cite `docs/documentation-audit/clean-slate-foundation/*` paths. Only audit JSONs reference these files.
- **`knip.json`** root entries: `tools/effect-language-service/compatibility.ts`, `tools/repository-paths/*`, `tools/quality-workflow/*`, 8 `tools/docs-deployment/*` entries, `tools/documentation/catalogue.runtime.ts`. Root project globs cover `tools/{effect-language-service,repository-paths,quality-workflow,docs-deployment}/**` and `tools/documentation/catalogue*.ts`. The `packages/scripts` workspace entry is release-readiness. **`knip.production.json`**: `packages/scripts` entries plus the `evidence.boundary.ts` ignore.
